problem: The question states as fact that 'contouring needs a sampled interpolator but point-to-point does not'. That is wrong on both sides. Contouring is regularly done with reference-pulse (incremental) interpolators driving steppers, as Section 3 itself says, and point-to-point servo drilling or punching tables commonly run a reference-word sampled position loop with no interpolation of a path. The real difference is coordination of the path, not sampled versus pulse.
fix: Reword Q6 as: 'Contouring needs each axis to be given a new coordinated position at every instant, while point-to-point does not. Explain.' Then the given answer (each axis simply runs to its target in point-to-point; in contouring every axis must be at the right point of the curve at a fixed update rate) fits correctly.

problem: The machining time is rounded to 3.61 s and then reused, so the axis pulse rates come out as 1662 and 1108 pulses/s and the check gives 1998 pulses/s. The check is written as if it 'matches' 2000, but the 2 pulses/s gap is only rounding, which can puzzle a student who recomputes.
fix: Carry more digits: t = 72.11 / 1200 = 0.06009 min = 3.606 s. Then X rate = 6000 / 3.606 = 1664 pulses/s and Y rate = 4000 / 3.606 = 1109 pulses/s; check √(1664² + 1109²) = 2000 pulses/s, exactly matching f = 1200 / (60 × 0.01) = 2000 pulses/s. Give the answers as 1664 and 1109 pulses/s.

problem: The text says the position loop 'decides the following error' but never says what following error is, so the term arrives undefined.
fix: Add: the following error is the small lag between the commanded position and the measured position while the axis is moving; the position loop gain sets how large it is allowed to be.
